title: How do we calculate these products quickly?
description: Four products of twenty five with twelve and with multiples of ten are found by making a hundred and by moving zeros, and a pair of numbers is found for a product of twelve crore. Each answer is then checked by another route.
teaching_notes: One idea: twenty five times four makes a hundred, and zeros can move from one factor to the other without changing the product. Ask the class what twenty five times four is before the first product is worked. Watch for students who give only one pair for the product of twelve crore and stop.

video_script.why: The child has used times ten and times a hundred with halving and dividing, and now makes a hundred from twenty five and moves zeros between factors.
video_script.substitution: Write one factor so that twenty five meets four to make 100, and move zeros between the two factors to keep the product the same.
video_script.payoff_line: Each product was found by making a hundred or by moving zeros

final_answer.spoken: three hundred, six thousand, thirty thousand, thirty thousand, and for example twelve hundred and one lakh

never_show: a final product before the answer beat
maths_rules: 12,00,00,000 is 12 followed by 7 zeros; 12 with 2 zeros times 1 with 5 zeros gives 1200 × 1,00,000; 12 with 3 zeros times 1 with 4 zeros gives 12,000 × 10,000; many pairs work
video_script.design: One idea: make a hundred from twenty five and four, and move zeros between factors. The anchor stays all video; the working band builds in the idea part; no hard clear.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>We must calculate these products quickly.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The first is twenty five times twelve. The second is twenty five times two hundred forty.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>The third is two hundred fifty times one hundred twenty. The fourth is two thousand five hundred times twelve.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>For the last one, we must find two numbers whose product is twelve crore.
<bookmark mark='m6'/>How can we calculate each of these without long multiplication?

beats.on_screen: the anchor holds still and gets an accent underline; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: cards: 25 × 4 = 100; moving zeros from one factor to the other keeps the product

marks.m2: the card for moving zeros appears with a zero sliding between two factors
marks.m3: the book example for times 5 appears faintly behind the cards

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Four twenty fives make one hundred, so twenty five times four is a good place to start.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Moving a zero from one number to the other leaves the product the same.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>We work the same way as the shortcut examples in your book.

marks.m1: the given line is written in the working band

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Given, four products, and a pair of blanks whose product is twelve crore.

beats.on_screen: To find: each product, and a pair for the blanks

marks.m1: the find line is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to calculate each product, and fill the blanks.

marks.m4: 25 × 24 = 25 × 4 × 6 = 100 × 6 is written, then one zero is added

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, for twenty five times twelve, write twelve as three times four.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Twenty five times four makes one hundred, so the product is one hundred times three.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>For twenty five times two hundred forty, write two hundred forty as twenty four times ten.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Twenty five times twenty four is one hundred times six. Then the factor ten adds one zero at the end.

marks.m4: an arrow marks the result of 25 × 12 with two zeros added

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, two hundred fifty is twenty five times ten, and one hundred twenty is twelve times ten.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Two hundred fifty times one hundred twenty equals twenty five times twelve, times one hundred.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Two thousand five hundred times twelve also equals twenty five times twelve, times one hundred.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Both take the result of the first product and add two zeros.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: 12 crore = 12 followed by 7 zeros; share the 7 zeros: 12 with 2 zeros × 1 with 5 zeros, or 12 with 3 zeros × 1 with 4 zeros

marks.m1: 12 crore is written as 12 followed by 7 zeros
marks.m2: the 7 zeros are drawn as seven small circles
marks.m3: the circles are shared 2 and 5, then 3 and 4

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, twelve crore is twelve followed by seven zeros.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>We can share the seven zeros between two numbers in many ways.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Give two zeros to twelve and five zeros to one. Or give three zeros to twelve and four zeros to one.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: check: 12 × 25 = 10 × 25 + 2 × 25 = 250 + 50; 240 × 25 = (240 × 100) ÷ 4 = 24,000 ÷ 4 = 5,000 + 1,000; the third and fourth each have 2 zeros after the digits of the first; 2 zeros + 5 zeros = 7 zeros and 3 zeros + 4 zeros = 7 zeros

marks.m1: the word check is written above four check lines
marks.m5: the third and fourth lines are marked with 2 zeros
marks.m6: 2 zeros + 5 zeros = 7 zeros and 3 zeros + 4 zeros = 7 zeros are written

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, check each answer by another route.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Twelve times twenty five is ten times twenty five plus two times twenty five. That is two hundred fifty plus fifty.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Two hundred forty times twenty five is two hundred forty times one hundred, divided by four.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Twenty four thousand divided by four is five thousand plus one thousand, which agrees.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>The third and fourth both have two zeros after the digits of the first, so they agree.
<bookmark mark='m6'/>For the last one, two zeros and five zeros make seven zeros. Three zeros and four zeros also make seven.

marks.m1: the five answers are written and boxed
marks.m2: the first four answers are lit one by one
marks.m3: the two example numbers for the blanks are lit

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Each product was found by making a hundred or by moving zeros.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The answers are three hundred, six thousand, thirty thousand and thirty thousand.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>For the last one, twelve hundred times one lakh is one example.
